items.title: Show HN: Fumble – keybr, but it learns from everything you type (macOS)
items.contentSnippet:
I love keybr, but it only sees the ten minutes a day I spend on keybr, not the ten hours I spend typing elsewhere. Can’t improve what you don’t measure.
(A)I made Fumble is a macOS menu-bar app that watches you type (all day, all local), works out which keys/key pairs are costing you time and gives you lessons built around them.

items.title: Show HN: Rhun, an open-source code editor written in assembly
items.contentSnippet:
I found that I'm not using even 1/3 of vim/vscode features anymore.
That's wht I'm building rhun - a small code editor for Linux, Windows and Apple silicon Macs. It obviously has Vim mode, a terminal, Git diffs and a panel for Claude Code or Codex sessions.

items.title: Show HN: What 482 hospitals charge vs. what insurers pay, from their own files
items.contentSnippet:
US hospitals must publish a machine-readable file of their prices, including the rate they've negotiated with each insurer. The files are huge (one is 36GB), in four formats and often messy, so almost nobody reads them.
I built a crawler that finds each hospital's official file and pulls out 29 common services. Across 482 hospitals: a moderate ER visit is listed at a median $1,285 while insurers pay $288; a metabolic panel is listed at $207 while insurers pay $11.46.

items.title: Show HN: Crookcooked – Open-source anti-theft alarm for Mac
items.contentSnippet:
I work from cafés and libraries a lot and hated leaving my MacBook alone for bathroom breaks, so I built crookcooked.
Arm it and the Mac locks. If someone messes with it, it screams, records them, and sends the clip plus a live view to your iPhone. Video is encrypted and sent over local network.
Open source, mostly vibe coded. I find myself using it quite often and thought it could be useful to other people as well!
